rows.note: This is the all-purpose casual choice for a duration such as 一個鐘.

example.english: I waited for you for a whole hour.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dang2 zo2 nei5 seng4 go3 zung1

rows.note: Use 鐘頭 as the fuller, unambiguous noun for a sixty-minute period.

example.english: This movie lasts an hour and a half.
example.traditional: 呢套戲足足有一個半鐘頭。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 zuk1 zuk1 jau5 jat1 go3 bun3 zung1 tau4

rows.note: Use 點 when a numeric time is being read as a clock time in ordinary speech rather than as strict formal military notation.

example.english: The meeting starts at eight thirty in the morning and lasts an hour.
example.traditional: 個會朝早八點三十分開始，做一個鐘。
example.jyutping: go3 wui6 ziu1 zou2 baat3 dim2 saam1 sap6 fan1 hoi1 ci2 zou6 jat1 go3 zung1

rows.note: Use 時 after a numeric time in formal or military-style time notation, as in 一千三百時.

example.english: The report says 1300 hours, one hour before the briefing.
example.traditional: 份報告寫住一千三百時，即係簡報前一個鐘。
example.jyutping: fan6 bou3 gou3 se2 zyu6 jat1 cin1 saam1 baak3 si4 zik1 hai6 gaan2 bou3 cin4 jat1 go3 zung1
